slice: Slice 1 — typed Address(kind, key) dataclass: converge emit/read/match on one address value-object, fixing cross-kind aliasing, slash-qualified mislift, and bare-target validation skip
thesis: Address handling today is scattered across five ad-hoc string helpers in three files, with two DISAGREEING split implementations and three suffix-matchers, which produces three confirmed defects: (a) colon-qualified refs alias across kinds via suffix-only matching, (b) emit slash-splits a declared-edge value that read qualifies, so the same value lifts to two different edges, and (c) bare declared-edge values skip emit-time validation entirely while read still lifts them. This slice introduces one frozen `atoms.Address(kind, key)` value-object with two constructors — `Address.parse` (self-describing colon/slash/bare, for the ref corpus) and `Address.for_edge` (declaration-qualified, SHARED by read-lift and emit — the convergence point) — plus exact `(kind, key)` tuple matching that replaces every suffix-matcher. The declaration licenses bare keys: emit adopts read's qualify behavior for declared edge fields; read never adopts emit's slash-splitting.
thesis_note: binding constraint discovered during research: 493 legacy-slash refs (kind/key, e.g. decision/atoms/n-on-fold-item) live in the project store and MUST keep matching — see risks and current_behavior

files.role: NEW — the Address(kind, key) frozen dataclass: `parse(raw)` (colon-first, then first-slash, then bare with kind=''), `for_edge(value, target_kind)` (colon→verbatim kind:key, else→(target_kind, whole value)), `__str__` → canonical 'kind:key'. Must be @dataclass(frozen=True) and stdlib-only (two atoms architecture ratchets enforce this).

current_behavior: EMIT (apps/loops/src/loops/commands/resolve.py): `_resolve_entity_refs` scans payload; for `ref` and declared-edge fields it comma-splits (1010-1014), then `_is_addr_candidate(addr)` (1017) requires a `:` or `/` separator (827-840), then `_resolve_one(addr)` (955-990) calls `_split_addr` (806-824) which splits colon-first, else first-slash. `_extract_edge_fields` (378-400) returns only `set[str]` of field NAMES — the target kind is discarded. Consequence: a declared-edge value `stakeholder=design/foo` is slash-split to kind=design,key=foo (defect b); a bare `stakeholder=acme` fails `_is_addr_candidate` and is silently skipped — no validation, no receipt edge line (defect c). READ (libs/engine/src/engine/vertex_reader.py): `_lift_edges` (1245-1267) calls `_normalize_edge_address(part, target_kind)` (1229-1242) which keeps colon verbatim else qualifies the WHOLE value with target_kind — so `design/foo`→`person:design/foo` (NOT split). Emit and read therefore disagree on the identical declared-edge value. MATCH (apps/loops/src/loops/surface.py): `_edge_corpus` (152-180) flattens item.refs (raw emitted strings — colon/legacy-slash/bare; confirmed 1587 colon, 493 legacy-slash, 73 bare in the live project store) and item.edges (already colon-normalized) into (address, predicate, source). `_address_matches_key(addr, key)` (274-276) matches `addr==key or addr.endswith('/'+key) or addr.endswith(':'+key)` — SUFFIX ONLY, kind-blind — so a corpus address `decision:design/foo` wrongly matches a `thread` row keyed `design/foo` (defect a). `_inbound_count` (342-372) duplicates the same three-form suffix scan inline over a flat `Counter[str]`, and has NO access to the target's kind (only item+key_field). `_compute_inbound_edges` (298) and `_inbound_predicates` (337) also route through `_address_matches_key`. Baseline: 186 loops tests + 22 engine edge tests pass; the aliasing behavior is currently LOCKED by test_fold_utils.py:156-174.

planned_changes.description: New libs/atoms/src/atoms/address.py: `@dataclass(frozen=True) class Address: kind: str; key: str`. `__str__` returns `f'{self.kind}:{self.key}'` when kind else the bare key. `@classmethod parse(cls, raw) -> Address|None`: strip; if empty→None; if ':' in v → split first ':' (colon binds tighter than key slashes), reject empty half → Address(kind,key); elif '/' in v → split FIRST '/' → Address(kind, key) [PRESERVES the 493 legacy-slash refs]; else → Address('', v) [bare, kind unknown]. `@classmethod for_edge(cls, value, target_kind) -> Address|None`: strip; if empty→None; if ':' in v → split first ':' → Address(kind,key); else → Address(target_kind, v) [declaration licenses the bare/slashed key — do NOT slash-split]. Export via __init__.py __all__ + _LAZY_IMPORTS.

In vertex_reader `_lift_edges`, replace `addr = _normalize_edge_address(part, target_kind); if addr:` with `a = Address.for_edge(part, target_kind); if a: edges.append(Edge(predicate=field_name, address=str(a)))`. Delete `_normalize_edge_address`. Read output is byte-identical for well-formed values (verified: str(Address(person,acme))=='person:acme', and colon-verbatim cases round-trip). Engine edge/lift tests should stay green UNCHANGED — treat any diff as a regression to investigate, not to accept.

Change return type to `dict[str,str]` mapping field→target: `return {edge.field: edge.target for edge in getattr(loop_def, 'edges', ())}`. EdgeDecl has `.field` and `.target` (libs/lang/src/lang/loader.py:441). emit.py:836 `else set()`→`else {}` (membership `r.field in edge_fields` is unchanged). resolve.py:1012 `field_name in local_edge_fields` is unchanged (dict key membership).

planned_changes.step: 4. Make emit resolution field-type-aware (fixes b + c)
planned_changes.description: In _resolve_entity_refs: rename local_edge_fields→local_edge_targets (dict). For each (field_name, addr): if field_name is a declared edge field → `address = Address.for_edge(addr, local_edge_targets[field_name])` and treat ANY non-empty/non-whitespace value as a candidate (declaration licenses bare — drop the separator requirement for this path); else (ref/general) → require separator via Address.parse and keep the whitespace/prose guard. Refactor `_resolve_one(addr)` to accept the pre-built Address (drop its internal `_split_addr`). Use the same Address for the unresolved-pin block (replaces `_split_addr` at 1025). Net: `_split_addr` and `_is_addr_candidate` dissolve into Address.parse/for_edge + a small per-path candidate check.

planned_changes.step: 5. Replace suffix-matchers with exact Address matching (fixes a)
planned_changes.description: In surface.py: (i) `_compute_inbound_refs` builds `Counter[Address]` by `Address.parse`-ing every corpus address (bare→Address('',key)). (ii) `_inbound_count(item, kind, key_field, inbound)` gains `kind`; returns `inbound[Address(kind,key)] + inbound[Address('', key)]` — O(1) exact lookup + bare fallback, replacing the three-form scan. (iii) `_inbound_predicates(item, kind, key_field, corpus)` gains `kind`; matches each corpus addr by `a=Address.parse(addr); (a.kind==kind and a.key==key) or (a.kind=='' and a.key==key)`. (iv) `_compute_inbound_edges` (already has section.kind) uses the same exact predicate; KEEP its output keyed by `_address(section.kind, key, id)` slash-form so the fetch.py graph consumer contract is unchanged. (v) delete `_address_matches_key`. (vi) `_candidate_addr_kind` → `Address.parse(v).kind or None` behind the existing empty/whitespace guard. Update call sites 581/601/614/634 to pass section.kind / w.section_kind.

acceptance_criteria: A single atoms.Address(kind, key) frozen dataclass is the only address parser/builder; `_split_addr`, `_is_addr_candidate`, `_normalize_edge_address`, and `_address_matches_key` are removed (dissolved into Address + per-path candidate checks) — residue swept, no dead helpers left
Defect (a) fixed: a colon- or slash-qualified corpus address matches ONLY a row of its own kind; decision:X and thread:X no longer cross-alias in ←counts, ←predicate breakdowns, or --refs adjacency
Defect (b) fixed: emit and read produce the SAME edge for a declared-edge value — `stakeholder=design/foo` → person:design/foo on both sides
Defect (c) fixed: a bare declared-edge value (`stakeholder=acme`) is validated at emit time and produces the inbound-edge receipt line, matching the edge read already lifts
Legacy-slash refs (kind/key) and bare refs continue to match exactly as before for their own kind — no regression to the 493 live slash-refs; read-lift output is byte-identical
Emit adopts read's bare-key interpretation for declared edge fields; read does NOT slash-split declared-edge values (Address.for_edge qualifies, never splits) — the direction's asymmetry holds
The fetch.py graph consumer contract is intact: `_compute_inbound_edges` still keys targets by the kind/key slash-form Row address
Full atoms + engine + loops suites green; goldens regenerated only after the ←N diff is confirmed to be intended de-aliasing
Address interface is compatible with future array-valued edge fields (a value is one Address; a set is a tuple of Address) but no array machinery is built (rider honored)
risks: LEGACY-SLASH BLAST RADIUS (highest): the live project store holds 493 kind-qualified slash refs (decision/atoms/..., thread/..., rfc/...). Address.parse MUST slash-split the ref/corpus population (colon-first, then FIRST slash) or these silently stop counting. The direction's 'read must not adopt slash-splitting' applies ONLY to the declared-edge population (Address.for_edge), NOT to self-describing refs. Do not 'simplify' Address.parse to drop the slash branch.

Two populations, two parse rules — this is deliberate, not duplication: refs are self-describing (parse), declared-edge values are declaration-qualified (for_edge). A reviewer may push to unify them; unifying would reintroduce defect (b). Document the boundary in Address docstrings.

GOLDEN DRIFT: exact matching lowers ←N wherever cross-kind colon aliasing currently over-counts. Any golden over a vertex with cross-kind key collisions will shift. Inspect each delta and confirm it is de-aliasing before --update-goldens; a count that changes in the wrong direction (legacy-slash dropping) is a bug.

open_questions: Should Edge.address (atoms/fold_state.py:33) BECOME an Address, or stay a canonical 'kind:key' str with Address used only as the internal parse/build/match value-object? Research recommends STR-STAYS: edge.address is consumed as a string in lenses/fold.py:1315 and fetch.py:330 and across the graph builder + goldens, so typing the field ripples widely for no defect-fixing benefit — Address 'carried through lift/corpus/matching' is satisfied by using it at the boundaries and stringifying into the stable field. But the spec wording ('a typed Address carried through typed-edge lift') admits the stronger reading, so this is the one genuine fork for the arbiter: contained-value-object (recommended) vs typed-field (wider blast radius, more 'honest' typing).

Is dropping legacy-slash-as-kind-qualified ever acceptable in exchange for a simpler single parse rule? Research says NO for this slice (493 live refs), but if a future slice migrates all slash refs to colon at rest (a store rewrite), Address.parse could shed its slash branch. Confirm the arbiter wants legacy-slash preserved indefinitely at read time vs scheduled for a one-time migration.
